channel.title: Pratik Dhanave — Blog
channel.description: Long-form writing on multi-agent AI, medical AI governance, HIPAA-aware architecture, and cloud-native systems.

item.title: Continuous Security: Monitoring, Compliance, and Culture
item.description: The capstone: shifting right to continuous security — runtime detection and vulnerability management as a loop, security observability and tamper-evident audit, compliance-as-code with evidence from the pipeline, metrics that matter, and the culture (paved roads, champions).

item.title: The Secure API Lifecycle
item.description: The capstone: baking security into the API lifecycle — shift-left threat modeling, CI gates (SAST, SCA, secret scanning, spec-driven authz/BOLA and DAST tests that fail the build), an OWASP-API-Top-10-to-control map, and incident response.

item.title: API Lifecycle and Governance
item.description: The capstone: designing and shipping consistent APIs at scale — the lifecycle, design review and style guides, linting the spec as policy-as-code in CI, contract testing so changes don't break consumers, an API catalog with ownership, and production observability.

item.title: Designing a System End to End
item.description: The capstone: one worked design end to end — requirements, estimation, API and data model, high-level architecture, and deep dives applying the whole series (scaling, caching, sharding, consistency, async, reliability) with explicit trade-offs.

item.title: AI Red-Teaming and Testing
item.description: Find AI security failures before attackers do: adversarial testing of the whole system, a test taxonomy mapped to the series, automated tooling (PyRIT, garak), a CI security-regression suite that fails the build, honest attack-success-rate measurement, and AI incident response.

item.title: Container and Kubernetes Security
item.description: Securing the runtime platform: minimal non-root images scanned for CVEs, the container isolation model and hardening (drop caps, read-only FS, seccomp), and Kubernetes — Pod Security Standards, RBAC, default-deny NetworkPolicies, and admission control (Gatekeeper/Kyverno).

item.title: API Gateways and Runtime Protection
item.description: The perimeter and runtime layer: the API gateway as a policy enforcement point (and why it can't replace per-service authz), WAF limits, improper inventory management (shadow/zombie APIs), security misconfiguration, and runtime detection.

item.title: Documentation and Developer Experience
item.description: An API is only as good as a developer's ability to succeed with it: OpenAPI as the machine-readable contract (docs, SDKs, mocks, contract tests), reference plus guides, errors as documentation, and optimizing time-to-first-successful-call.

item.title: Reliability and Resilience
item.description: Designing systems that survive failure: the nines and SLI/SLO/error budgets, eliminating single points of failure, timeouts and retries with backoff+jitter made safe by idempotency, circuit breakers, rate limiting and load shedding, and graceful degradation.

item.title: Building an AI Governance Program
item.description: The capstone: assemble a right-sized governance program — roles and accountability, a model/use-case inventory as the backbone, lifecycle gates, and policy-as-code that blocks deploy when an owner, risk tier, model card, eval pass, or monitor is missing.

item.title: Securing the AI Pipeline
item.description: DevSecOps for AI: secrets in a manager not code, least-privilege runtime identities (no ambient prod creds for agents), egress control, rate/spend limits against model DoS, supply-chain verification in CI, prompts-as-code, and a security-eval gate that fails the build.

item.title: Production on watsonx
item.description: Run a watsonx system in production from Python: IBM Cloud vs Cloud Pak for Data, project_id vs deployment spaces, reliability (tenacity retries, IAM token refresh, fallback), token-based cost, observability wired to watsonx.governance monitors, and securing IAM credentials.

item.title: Production on the NVIDIA Stack
item.description: Run an NVIDIA-stack LLM system in production from Python: hosted vs self-hosted vs hybrid, reliability (client retries, tenacity backoff, readiness probes, fallback), the GPU-hours cost model, Prometheus observability across the pipeline, and securing nvapi-/NGC keys.

item.title: Infrastructure as Code Security and Policy as Code
item.description: Securing infrastructure definitions and enforcing guardrails automatically: IaC scanning (Checkov/tfsec/Trivy) for misconfig, drift detection, and policy-as-code with OPA/Rego + Conftest so org rules block bad infra before apply — not in a wiki.

item.title: Transport and Data Security
item.description: Protecting data in transit and at rest: TLS everywhere (even internal, zero-trust), mTLS for service-to-service, minimizing sensitive data exposure, encryption at rest with managed keys, secrets management, a correct CORS allow-list, and redacting logs.

item.title: Beyond REST: GraphQL and gRPC
item.description: When REST isn't the right shape: GraphQL (client-selected fields, and its N+1 / caching / complexity costs) and gRPC (Protobuf, HTTP/2, streaming, codegen) — plus a decision framework for REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC.

item.title: Asynchronous Processing and Messaging
item.description: Decoupling with queues and events: message queues vs pub/sub vs log-based streaming, delivery semantics (why exactly-once delivery is a myth — do idempotent processing), ordering, backpressure, the transactional outbox, and dead-letter queues.

item.title: The AI Regulatory Landscape
item.description: Orient in AI regulation and translate it into controls (not legal advice): the EU AI Act's risk tiers and obligations, ISO/IEC 42001 as a certifiable AI management system, NIST AI RMF, and a crosswalk mapping each obligation to the artifact that satisfies it.

item.title: Guardrails and Content Safety
item.description: The defensive layer that screens inputs and outputs: input/output/topical/groundedness rails, the real ecosystem (Llama Guard, Granite Guardian, NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI, Presidio, hosted moderation), and a vendor-neutral guardrail pipeline — with honest false-positive/negative trade-offs.

item.title: Governance and Monitoring with watsonx.governance
item.description: Governance is why many enterprises pick watsonx: model inventory, automated factsheets, monitoring (quality, drift, bias, and generative metrics like faithfulness), explainability, and EU AI Act-aligned risk workflows — with the ibm-watsonx-gov evaluation SDK and what to log.

item.title: Self-Hosting and Optimizing Inference
item.description: Move from the hosted API Catalog to self-hosted inference: run a NIM container (your Python client works unchanged by swapping base_url), use Triton directly via tritonclient, and understand the TensorRT-LLM levers — quantization, in-flight batching, paged KV cache, tensor parallelism.

item.title: Bedrock in Production: IAM, Cost, and Observability
item.description: Taking a Bedrock Go service to production: least-privilege IAM and role-based credentials, tuning the SDK's built-in retryer for throttling, token-based cost tracking, and observability via model-invocation logging, structured metrics, and request IDs.

item.title: Secrets Management: Keeping Credentials Out of Code and Under Control
item.description: Keeping credentials out of code and under control: the bad-to-good hierarchy, secrets managers (Vault/KMS), dynamic short-lived secrets, rotation that consumers actually pick up, and workload identity / OIDC so CI and services never store a long-lived key.

item.title: Rate Limiting and Resource Consumption
item.description: Rate limiting as a security control (OWASP API4/API6): the algorithms and their trade-offs, keying on authenticated identity not just IP, 429 + Retry-After, protecting expensive operations, and defending sensitive business flows from bulk abuse.

item.title: Versioning and Evolution: Changing an API Without Breaking Its Consumers
item.description: Changing an API without breaking consumers: what counts as breaking, versioning strategies and their trade-offs (URI vs header vs additive evolution), the robustness principle and its limits, and responsible deprecation with Sunset headers and usage telemetry.

item.title: Consistency, Availability, and Consensus
item.description: The theory that governs distributed data, stated correctly: CAP as a partition-time choice (not pick-2-of-3), PACELC, the consistency spectrum with what-the-user-sees examples, quorums, and consensus/Raft at an intuition level.

item.title: Monitoring and Drift in Production
item.description: Governance doesn't stop at deploy — the Manage function in production: what to monitor (operational, quality, safety), detecting drift including silent provider-model drift behind moving aliases, and the audit trail (versions + retrieved context, PII-redacted) that becomes regulatory evidence.

item.title: RAG and Supply-Chain Security
item.description: Securing the components around the model: RAG as an injection and poisoning vector (treat retrieved content as hostile, enforce provenance and per-user authz) and supply-chain risk (safetensors over pickle, model provenance, pinned and vetted dependencies and tools).

item.title: Guardrails and Granite Guardian
item.description: Add safety to a watsonx app in Python with two layers: built-in HAP/PII moderations on generation, and Granite Guardian — IBM's dedicated risk models — run as a classifier to screen input and check RAG groundedness, wrapped in a guarded-generate flow.

item.title: Guardrails with NeMo Guardrails
item.description: Add safety with NeMo Guardrails, in-process in Python: the rail types (input/output/dialog/retrieval), the config.yml + Colang model, loading with RailsConfig/LLMRails backed by a NIM model, and detecting when a rail trips instead of treating a refusal as a normal answer.

item.title: Guardrails and Safety
item.description: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock in Go: content filters, denied topics, PII/sensitive-information filters, and contextual grounding — attaching a guardrail to a Converse call and screening arbitrary text with ApplyGuardrail, checking for intervention.

item.title: Production AI
item.description: The capstone: running an LLM system in production from a Go engineer's seat — reliability (timeouts, retries, fallbacks), security (injection, least-privilege tools, secrets), cost and observability, CI eval gates, and versioning models and prompts.

item.title: Software Supply Chain Security and SBOMs
item.description: Securing everything you didn't write: SCA for known-vulnerable dependencies, the supply-chain threat model (typosquatting, dependency confusion, build compromise), SBOMs (SPDX/CycloneDX), and provenance/integrity with SLSA and Sigstore signing.

item.title: Input Validation and Injection
item.description: Treating every input as hostile: schema/DTO validation (allow-list, reject unknown fields), injection defenses (parameterized queries), and SSRF — allow-listing destinations and blocking internal/link-local ranges including via redirects.

item.title: Errors and Idempotency: The Two Things That Make an API Safe to Build On
item.description: The two things that make an API safe to build on: a consistent machine-readable error model (RFC 9457 problem+json, stable error codes, no leaked internals) and idempotency (the Idempotency-Key pattern so retries don't double-charge).

item.title: Databases and Storage
item.description: Choosing and scaling the data layer: relational vs NoSQL by access pattern, indexing (B-tree/hash/LSM), normalization vs denormalization, replication, partitioning/sharding and the shard-key decision, and the distributed-transaction trade-off.

item.title: Bias, Fairness, and Explainability
item.description: The trustworthy-AI properties regulators care about: where bias enters, why fairness notions conflict (you must choose one), disaggregated evaluation, mitigation with Fairlearn/AIF360, and explainability (SHAP/LIME) — with the honest caveat that LLM rationales are not faithful explanations.

item.title: Insecure Output Handling and Excessive Agency
item.description: Two OWASP risks that turn an injection into damage: insecure output handling (model output is untrusted input — never eval/shell/SQL it unescaped) and excessive agency (least-privilege tools, allow-lists, human approval for irreversible actions, audit logs).

item.title: RAG on watsonx
item.description: Build a full RAG pipeline in Python on watsonx: chunk (with Docling for parsing), embed and store, retrieve, rerank, and generate a grounded, cited answer with a Granite model — shown both from scratch and via the idiomatic langchain-ibm assembly, with notes on scaling to watsonx.data/Milvus.

item.title: RAG on the NVIDIA Stack
item.description: Build a full RAG pipeline in Python on NVIDIA's stack: chunk and embed with NeMo Retriever, shortlist by cosine, rerank, then generate a grounded, cited answer with ChatNVIDIA — shown both from scratch and the idiomatic LangChain assembly, with notes on scaling to a vector DB.

item.title: Bedrock Agents
item.description: Agents for Amazon Bedrock from Go: the managed reason-act loop that runs server-side (vs the DIY Converse loop), invoking an agent alias with InvokeAgent, streaming the response and trace events, and keeping multi-turn state with a SessionId.

item.title: Inference Optimization
item.description: Make LLM systems faster and cheaper without retraining: TTFT vs throughput, exact and semantic response caching, prompt caching, token reduction, model routing and cascades, and Go concurrency with a worker pool and rate limiter.

item.title: Evaluating Multi-Turn and Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: The capstone of the Evaluating Agents in Go series: how to score a conversation instead of a single reply, how to attribute errors across a coordinator and its sub-agents, and how to build rubric, safety,...

item.title: SAST, DAST, and Security Testing in CI
item.description: Automated security testing in the pipeline: SAST vs DAST vs IAST and their trade-offs, secret scanning (including git history), where each runs, and making findings actionable so false-positive fatigue doesn't get the scanner muted.

item.title: Authorization: BOLA, BFLA, and Object-Level Access
item.description: The dominant class of API bugs: broken object level authorization (BOLA/IDOR — the #1 API risk), broken function level authorization, and object property level (mass assignment / excessive data exposure) — with allow-listed DTOs, ownership checks, and deny-by-default.

item.title: Requests, Responses, and Pagination
item.description: Shaping the payloads clients consume: consistent naming, dates and money done right, content negotiation, field selection, and pagination — why offset pagination breaks at scale and how cursor/keyset pagination fixes it.

item.title: Caching
item.description: Caching as the highest-leverage latency tool — and its hardest problem: where caches live, the patterns (cache-aside/read-through/write-through/write-behind), eviction, and invalidation including cache stampede, penetration, and hot keys.

item.title: Evaluation and Quality Gates
item.description: Governance enforced through evaluation — the Measure function made real: build a versioned eval set, pick the metric families (quality, faithfulness, safety, bias, PII, cost/latency), and turn eval into a CI quality gate that fails the build on regression.

item.title: Data Security and Privacy
item.description: Protecting data in LLM systems: sensitive-information disclosure, PII in prompts and logs (your observability can be the leak), redaction with Presidio, data residency, and per-user access control on the retrieval layer so RAG doesn't leak across tenants.

item.title: Embeddings and Reranking with watsonx
item.description: Use watsonx.ai's slate embedding models and reranking from Python to build RAG's retrieval core: embed_documents vs embed_query, numpy cosine scoring, and a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipeline — plus the langchain-ibm WatsonxEmbeddings/WatsonxRerank path.
